subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write notes on the working of the heart of man.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.12, LAQ 2. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Action potentials
steps.why: The heart is not told to beat by a nerve: the signal starts inside the heart itself, in the nodal tissue.
common_mistakes: Writing that a nerve starts each beat. The SAN does.
Naming only the cardiac cycle. Four phases are asked.
steps.memory_tip: Signal, cycle, output, circulation — the four phases in order.
steps.margin_note: Name all four phases first, then take them one by one.
lines: The working of the heart has 4 phases:
1. Generation and conduction of action
potentials
2. Cardiac cycle
3. Cardiac output
4. Double circulation
The contractions of the heart chambers are
due to the action potential generated by
the nodal tissue, the SAN.

steps.label: The cardiac cycle
steps.why: One beat is one full round of the same three events, so defining the cycle sets up everything that follows.
common_mistakes: Defining the cycle as one contraction. It runs from one beat to the start of the next.
Giving no duration. 0.8 s is a marked figure.
steps.margin_note: Definition, duration, then the three phases named.
lines: The cardiac events that occur from the
beginning of one heart beat to the
beginning of the next form the cardiac
cycle. It lasts about 0.8 seconds.
It has 3 phases: atrial systole, ventricular
systole and cardiac diastole.

steps.label: Atrial systole
steps.why: The ventricles are already almost full before the atria contract, so this contraction is only a top-up of about thirty per cent.
common_mistakes: Writing that the atria fill the ventricles completely. They add about 30%.
Giving the wrong time. Atrial systole lasts about 0.1 s.
steps.memory_tip: The atria only top the ventricles up: 0.1 second, 30 per cent.
steps.margin_note: Three short points: what, how long, how much.
lines: The SAN generates an action potential which
makes both atria contract together. This is
atrial systole.
It lasts about 0.1 s.
It increases the flow of blood into the
ventricles by about 30%.
The rest of the blood had already flowed in
before the atrial systole.

steps.label: Ventricular systole
steps.why: The atrioventricular valves shut the moment ventricular pressure passes atrial pressure, which is what stops blood going backwards.
common_mistakes: Writing that the atria contract at the same time. They relax.
Leaving out the AVN as the relay centre.
steps.memory_tip: AVN relays, bundle of His carries, ventricles squeeze.
steps.margin_note: Follow the signal: AVN, bundle of His, Purkinje fibres.
lines: The action potential reaches the AVN, which
acts as a relay centre.
The impulses pass through the bundle of His
and the Purkinje fibres and cause
ventricular systole.
It lasts about 0.3 s.
The atria relax during ventricular systole.

steps.label: The heart sounds
steps.why: Each sound is a valve slamming shut, so the two sounds mark the two moments when blood is stopped from running back.
common_mistakes: Saying the sounds come from the muscle contracting. They come from valves closing.
Swapping them. Lub is the AV valves, dup the semilunar valves.
steps.memory_tip: Lub = AV valves shut; dup = semilunar valves shut.
steps.margin_note: Tie each sound to the valve that makes it.
lines: Rising pressure closes the atrioventricular
valves and prevents backflow of blood.
This produces the first heart sound, 'lub'.
As the ventricular pressure rises further,
the semilunar valves open and blood flows
into the aortic arches.

steps.label: Cardiac diastole
steps.why: The longest part of the beat is the rest, which is when the heart muscle receives its own blood supply.
common_mistakes: Giving diastole the shortest time. It is the longest, 0.4 s.
Forgetting the second heart sound here.
steps.memory_tip: The heart rests longer than it works: 0.4 s of the 0.8 s.
steps.margin_note: Relaxation, valve closure, sound, then the joint diastole.
lines: The ventricles now relax and the
ventricular pressure falls.
This closes the semilunar valves and
prevents backflow of blood.
It lasts about 0.4 s.
It produces the second heart sound, 'dup'.
All four chambers are now relaxed together.
This is the joint diastolic phase.

steps.label: Cardiac output
steps.why: Stroke volume is one squeeze and cardiac output is a minute of squeezes, so the second is simply the first times the heart rate.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two up. Stroke volume is per beat, output is per minute.
Leaving out the working. The multiplication carries the mark.
steps.memory_tip: 70 mL a beat, 72 beats a minute, about 5 litres a minute.
steps.margin_note: Write the equation on its own line.
lines: The volume of blood pumped out by each
ventricle in one heart beat is the stroke
volume.
The volume pumped out by each ventricle in
one minute is the cardiac output.

lines.text: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate

steps.label: Double circulation
steps.why: Blood passes through the heart twice in one full round, which is what keeps the oxygenated and deoxygenated streams from mixing.
common_mistakes: Writing that blood passes through the heart once. It passes twice.
Naming only one of the two circulations.
steps.memory_tip: Right side to the lungs, left side to the body.
steps.margin_note: Two named circulations, then the reason it matters.
lines: Pulmonary circulation: blood from the right
ventricle goes to the lungs through the
pulmonary arteries, is aerated, and returns
to the left atrium by the pulmonary veins.
Systemic circulation: the left ventricle
pumps blood through the systemic arch to
all parts of the body, and the venae cavae
bring it back to the right atrium.

lines.text: Blood passes through the heart twice

insider_note: The three durations — 0.1 s, 0.3 s, 0.4 s adding to 0.8 s — are the easiest marks in this answer and the ones most often left out.
